resolution_rule: Use ONLY first BEA Personal Income and Outlays October 2026 report's seasonally adjusted core PCE price index excluding food and energy month-over-month percentage change as printed to one decimal. Scheduled Nov 25 2026 08:30 EST, else first actual official release. TRUE iff first printed October value >=+0.4%, else FALSE. If source omits this specific monthly core measure, remain pending. Never substitute core CPI, core-core PPI, headline PCE, YoY, unofficial nowcasts, revisions or future consensus. Frozen p=.40 and point +.3% and 80% [.1%,.5%] and frozen two point +.3% benchmarks; score proper Brier/log, absolute error, interval hit/width and comparable frozen benchmark point errors. Preserve original fields and record revisions separately.
rationale: BLS October 10 core CPI +.3% is an already-observed consumer price measure, but BEA core PCE uses distinct basket weights; producer core-core PPI +.5% (November 13 initial release) can affect components differently.
Contemporaneous November 13 Reuters commentary and November 10 Conference Board estimate point near +.3% monthly core PCE; threshold >=+.4% is an upside transmission test, not the base case.

H001/H003 remain equally weighted .39, so p=.40 is judgmental and not a calibrated homogeneous PCE frequency. Even a +.4 print cannot alone prove H003 because weighted PCE pathways and policy effects may offset.
An eventual downside core-PCE print despite sticky narrow PPI would challenge mechanical pass-through, while a high print would challenge overly rapid normalization; retain competing mechanisms.
No claim of point advantage: both frozen September no-change and external point are also +.3%. No trading or post-hoc benchmark switching.
surprising_if: First BEA October 2026 core PCE m/m >= +0.6% above nominal 80% upper interval.
First BEA October core PCE m/m <=0.0% below nominal 80% lower interval.
